verdict.label: Full review
verdict.summary: You can test immediately using Composio's managed app, but custom Gmail OAuth requires creating a project in the Google API Console, configuring scopes, and completing Google OAuth verification for sensitive scopes.

composioFit.summary: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Gmail by default, allowing you to build and iterate immediately without registering your own app. You can switch to a custom auth config if you need custom branding, scopes, or dedicated rate limits.
whyOwnApp: You need your own app name on OAuth consent screens.
You need custom scopes not covered by Composio's defaults.
You are hitting shared rate limits and need a dedicated quota.

phases.name: Create Google Cloud Project & App
steps: Go to the Google API Console and create a Google Cloud project.
Select the Web application application type for server-side usage.
Obtain your Client ID and Client Secret.
phases.handoff: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret from the Google API Console.

phases.name: Configure Auth Config in Composio
steps: Navigate to the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Choose OAuth2 as the auth scheme for Gmail.
Copy the redirect URI provided by Composio and paste it into the Google API Console.
phases.handoff: Save the Client ID and Client Secret back into the Composio dashboard.

phases.name: Test Connection
steps: Initialize a session and test the Gmail toolkit using your own account.
phases.handoff: Verify tokens are refreshing properly and API calls succeed.

phases.name: Google OAuth Verification
steps: Submit app verification request to remove the unverified app warning if using sensitive scopes for public users.

artefacts.body: Our AI agent application requires access to Gmail to assist users with reading, drafting, and organizing emails securely via Composio toolkits.

requirements.when: Required for OAuth app publishing and sensitive scope verification.

requirements.label: OAuth Verification
requirements.when: Required if your public application uses sensitive or restricted scopes.

scopes.purpose: View your email messages and settings.
Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account.

redirectRules.rule: Must use the exact redirect URI provided in the Composio dashboard when configuring credentials in the Google API Console.

blockers.cause: The OAuth client ID was not found or is invalid in the Google API Console.
blockers.fix: Check that the Client ID entered in the Composio dashboard matches your Google Cloud project credentials exactly.
blockers.fallback: Use Composio's managed Gmail app instead of a custom auth config.

blockers.symptom: Unverified app warning screen shown to users during consent.
blockers.cause: The app requests sensitive scopes and has not completed Google's OAuth verification process.
blockers.fix: Submit an app verification request through the Google API Console.
blockers.fallback: Use Composio-managed apps which handle standard consent branding.

blockers.symptom: Older refresh tokens stop working unexpectedly.
blockers.cause: The application requested enough refresh tokens to exceed limits per client-user combination or per user across all clients.
blockers.fix: Save refresh tokens securely in long-term storage and reuse them instead of repeatedly requesting new ones.
blockers.fallback: Re-authenticate the user to obtain a fresh refresh token.

checklist.text: Create a Google Cloud project in the Google API Console.
Choose the Web application application type for server-side app interactions.
Obtain your OAuth 2.0 client credentials (Client ID and Client Secret).
Navigate to the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Register the Composio redirect URI in your Google Cloud project console.
Save the Client ID and Client Secret back into the Composio dashboard.
Test the connection with your own account and verify token refresh logic.
Submit for Google OAuth verification if using sensitive scopes for public production users.

uncertainties: Exact turnaround time for Google OAuth verification review is not explicitly documented in the sources and may vary.
Specific rate limit numerical quotas per client are not detailed in the source texts.
